title: Cycle 22: Local auth observability + proactive refresh + recovery UI
weak_spots: No visibility into local-auth token health or refresh history
Reactive-only refresh means first request after sleep may fail with 403
No audit trail for token lifecycle events
No manual recovery UI when token refresh fails
Blunt LocalAuthError.fetchFailed had no status code
competitors: SwiftAI Boilerplate AsyncStream AuthState + proactive 60s-before-expiry refresh
TokenEater AppErrorState enum + menu-bar recovery banner + silent keychain reads
omi AuthSessionCoordinator single-flight refresh + definitive death classifier
Ory token lifecycle management + refresh-token rotation + family invalidation
onelake-explorer-macos Sign In Again menu-bar action

variants.name: Observability + proactive refresh + recovery UI
variants.summary: LocalAuthMonitor tracks state/metadata/audit log; provider refreshes proactively after 5 min; Queen status UI shows health and Refresh/Reset actions.

variants.name: Server-side token metadata + TTL
variants.summary: BrowserOS exposes issuedAt/expiresIn; TriOS refreshes at 75% TTL and shows countdown. Needs server changes.

variants.name: Biometric-gated high-value actions
variants.summary: Protect Keychain item with SecAccessControl; require biometric for reset. Strongest anti-exfiltration but prompts user.

lessons: Keep audit logs token-free by design: store event names and reasons, never the secret value.
Actor-isolated monitor + MainActor UIManager separates telemetry from UI control without exposing the provider globally.
Proactive refresh should be threshold-injectable so tests can force/stop it deterministically.
Status components need a consistent action parameter name; mismatching actionLabel vs action caused a swiftc error.
